reference: Rukhin, A. L. Information-type divergence when the likelihood ratios are bounded. Applicationes Mathematicae 24(4), 415-423, 1997. DOI 10.4064/am-24-4-415-423.
result: Theorem 2.1: a bound on the likelihood ratio implies upper bounds on f-divergences between two distributions, for f with a minimum at 1 and bowl-shaped (non-increasing on (0,1), non-decreasing on (1,inf)).
difference: Their bound is a general f-divergence bound under a likelihood-ratio constraint. P6a is the pairwise log-ratio shift bounded by R and P6b a total-variation bound; both are one-line consequences here. Whether P6b follows as a special case of Theorem 2.1 has NOT been checked, because the theorem has not been read.
claim_consequence: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-04. The previous NOT_FOUND_NEEDS_HUMAN was a factual error about the world: the reference exists, and multiple independent sources reproduce the same title, journal, volume, issue, pages, year and DOI, and describe Theorem 2.1. The FULL TEXT WAS NOT READ -- every publisher host is blocked from this environment -- so the theorem's exact hypotheses have not been compared against P6. CONSEQUENCE UNCHANGED: no sharpness may be claimed for P6b. Sharpness is asserted for Rukhin's own bound by secondary description, which is NOT the same statement as sharpness of our specialization, and the two must not be conflated. Cite as the bounded-likelihood-ratio antecedent for P6a/P6b and state that our bound is an elementary specialization, not a restatement.

reference: Athanasopoulou, E., Li, L. and Hadjicostis, C. N. Maximum Likelihood Failure Diagnosis in Finite State Machines Under Unreliable Observations. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control 55(3), 579-593, 2010.
result: Recursive algorithm choosing the most likely deterministic FSM given an observation sequence corrupted by insertions, deletions and transpositions with known probabilities. Later extended with bounds on the probability of misclassification.

There is no corruption distribution to know.
claim_consequence: Cite as the closest ML-diagnosis-under-unreliable-observation work and state the noise-versus-applicability distinction explicitly. Do NOT claim CSIA handles a case they cannot; claim it is a different mechanism.

claim_consequence: Cite as the fixed-mask case and state that the time-varying, fault-coupled mask is what differs. That difference is shared with the state-dependent-observation literature, which already owns it -- so this is not a novelty claim either.
